title: TT-Bio: biomolecular structure, design and embeddings on Tenstorrent
subtitle: Five structure-prediction models at 512 residues, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200 and B200.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

One cell per model per platform, holding the fastest measured arm that passes parity against its own reference. Every Tenstorrent cell states which parity it holds: bit-exact, byte-identical, or a measured structural delta inside a bar that was fixed before the number existed. A cell with no measurement gets status 'blocked' and a reason. Do not fill it with an estimate.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm folds, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same two input files on both sides, each model at its own recycle and sampling-step settings. Each Tenstorrent cell is that model's fastest arm that passes parity.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is this page's assumption for how long an AI accelerator earns its keep: one year shorter than the general-purpose server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q, because an accelerator generation lasts about two years. A shorter window favours the cheaper box, so the range below brackets it.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Throughput per dollar, with the DGX H200 set to 1.00x, on two bases. Purchase price: predictions per hour / price, with no amortisation window, because the window cancels from that ratio. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour / cost per hour, where cost per hour = price / (4 x 8766 h) + power kW x $/kWh.
cost_model.sensitivity: Shift the window to 3 or 6 years, or the rate to the 13.54 c/kWh US commercial tariff, and the Tenstorrent figure moves between 2.47x and 3.71x. It does not invert.

b200.detail: The fold hangs after featurization and never completes, inside the cuEquivariance triangle kernels. Protenix-v2 pins cuequivariance-ops-torch 0.8.0; turning off fusion, the shared-vars cache and TF32 does not clear it. No number is estimated for this cell.

p150a.parity: 0.3248 A CA RMSD, inside the 0.35 A bar fixed before the measurement
p150a.ref: Median of three warm folds on one p150a, 82.942 / 82.880 / 82.960 s, spread 0.080 s, measured uninstrumented on the shipped path. The earlier 87.1 s in this cell was a subtraction, not a measurement, and it was 4.158 s stale. This is the one cell that is not bit-exact: the triangle-attention matmul folds its contraction in twelve-tile blocks, worth one bf16 unit in the last place, so the CIF digest moves 50aa1e46583bd5a8 to 357c67003bb738ac and plDDT 0.754131 to 0.754110. The structural cost is 0.3248 A Kabsch CA, measured on a monomeric 298-residue control because this fixture's two domains hinge freely and saturate the metric. The byte-identical arm at the same two matmul settings returns 88.61 s.

h200.ref: Median of n=3, spread 0.29 %. opendde 1.0.3, torch 2.7.1+cu128, plDDT 0.827.

b200.detail: The same hang, same signature. OpenDDE pins cuequivariance-ops-torch 0.10.0. The three models that run clean on the B200 all resolve 0.11.1, so the split follows the cuEquivariance version rather than the model.

p150a.ref: Four warm folds of the shipped default on main after the merge, one process under benchlock on qb2 card 3 (perf/of3x3/ab_512_postmerge_qb2c3.json): 44.512 / 44.577 / 44.559 / 44.451 s, median 44.535, spread 0.126 s. The lever is TriangleAttention's fp32-softmax tail run height-sharded in L1 instead of DRAM-interleaved, merged from wk/openfold3-to-3x-perdollar; the control arm without it, in an alternating run on the branch, is 51.19 s. Bit-exact: CIF sha256 da9b4ed68f8c0405 and plDDT 0.547851 on all four folds, the same digest the control arm produced, and it holds at 768 and 1024 aa too.

h200.ref: Median of n=3, spread 0.21 %. openfold3 0.4.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130, checkpoint of3-p2-155k.pt, plDDT 0.639.

design.deck: BoltzGen and RFdiffusion3, seconds per binder design on one AI Processor, each on its own pinned target.
design.cond: Wall-clock seconds to return one binder design on a single AI Processor, warm, at each model's shipped defaults. Shorter is better. Both sides run the same target and ask for the same designs; RFdiffusion3's eight come out of one forward of 8 on the GPUs and eight forwards of 1 on the p150a, the fastest batch measured at this target.
design.note: No throughput-per-dollar figure is derived here. The rung above this one overflows L1 on the p150a for BoltzGen, so BoltzGen is measured one rung below it, where the H200 sits at 41 % of its power limit and the B200 at 31 %, and a cost ratio taken on an idle GPU would not survive a bigger target. On both models the B200 is no faster than the H200, 0.6 % slower on RFdiffusion3 and 1.27x slower on BoltzGen. The rows above carry a bit-exact digest; a design draws a new sequence every time, so these two carry per-run output validation instead, and every design counted here wrote, parsed, had finite coordinates and had the residue topology its spec asked for.
design.methods: Two pinned targets, one per model, at the shipped defaults: BoltzGen 500 sampling steps at batch 1, RFdiffusion3 200 timesteps for eight designs. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians on one Blackhole p150a under a run lock, with the cold pass and, for BoltzGen, the design that pays the checkpoint switch dropped. GPU figures come from the same protocol on rented single-GPU nodes. Designs are validated per run rather than digested: chain sizes, residue topology and finite coordinates, never atom equality between siblings, because sibling designs legitimately differ.

models.name: BoltzGen
models.target: EBV gp350 D123 (9ma0 chain A), 414 target residues, 100-residue binder, 514 tokens

p150a.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, 45.187 / 45.221 / 45.357 / 45.393 s, spread 0.46 %, with a second independent process 0.05 % away at 45.265 s. qb2, Blackhole p150a physical card 0, ttnn 0.68.0, under a run lock. End-to-end per design; the cold design and the design that pays the 1.9 GB checkpoint switch are dropped, the same two the GPU arm drops. 500 sampling steps resolved from the shipped design.yaml and asserted per design. 20.501 s of each design is the denoising loop at 41.00 ms per step, the other 24.8 s is trunk, post-processing and writing.

h200.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, spread 1.18 %, end-to-end per design. boltzgen 0.1.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, fused kernels on. The cold design and the design that pays the checkpoint switch are dropped.

b200.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, spread 0.59 %, end-to-end per design, same stack.

models.name: RFdiffusion3
models.target: Human serum albumin (9q6y chain A), 585 target residues, 100-residue binder, 6051 atoms

p150a.ref: Median of n=2 warm forwards, 123.501 / 123.490 s per forward of 1, spread 0.01 %, 617.5 ms per timestep. qb2, Blackhole p150a physical card 0, ttnn 0.68.0, under a run lock. The run asked for the shipped batch of 8; the runtime runs 1 at this target size, because batching stops paying above 2952 atoms and the batch of 2 the atom-pair budget used to admit here is 1.16x slower per design. Matmul program-config calibration is also on by default above that size, worth 1.166x here and bitwise identical to the uncalibrated path, same CIF digest 9c49ab6f36267950358d0cdcfa93abe9. All three designs wrote 6051 atoms and 685 residues and passed validation.

h200.ref: Median of n=3 warm batches, 103.79 s per batch of 8, spread 0.29 %. rc-foundry 0.2.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, 553.1 W, 79.0 % of the box's own 700 W limit.

b200.ref: Median of n=3 warm batches, 104.39 s per batch of 8, spread 1.34 %, same stack.

eia-industrial.label: US EIA, Electric Power Monthly, table 5.3
eia-industrial.detail: US average retail price of electricity to the industrial sector, 8.71 cents/kWh for May 2026, released 2026-07-23. The commercial-sector price for the same month is 13.54 cents/kWh and is used in the sensitivity check.

amzn-10q.label: Amazon, Form 10-Q, useful life of servers
amzn-10q.detail: From 1 January 2025 Amazon depreciates a subset of its servers and networking equipment over five years, down from six, citing the pace of AI hardware development. This page's four-year window is one year shorter than that.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware.
Accuracy is not compared here. Each stack ran its own settings and every run was checked against its own plDDT, but these numbers are wall-clock and cost.
